name: De La Soul
hook: Three high school friends whose collage of samples and offbeat humor gave the Native Tongues collective its founding record.
blurb: Kelvin 'Posdnuos' Mercer, David 'Trugoy' Jolicoeur and Vincent 'Maseo' Mason formed De La Soul in high school in Amityville, Long Island. Producer Prince Paul heard their demo tape and brought them to Tommy Boy Records. Their 1989 debut, '3 Feet High and Rising', built playful, densely sampled songs out of everything from James Brown to a Johnny Cash title, French-language lesson records and game-show interludes, tied together by comic skits rather than one story, and it reset what people thought a sample could be. They were part of the Native Tongues, a loose group of like-minded rap acts that included A Tribe Called Quest, and appeared together on the 'Buddy' remix that year. Not all those samples were cleared: in 1991 the Turtles, a psychedelic pop group, sued over an uncredited use, and it was settled out of court. Trugoy died in February 2023.

signatureTracks.title: Me Myself and I
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Their breakout single, pushing back against being cast as hip-hop hippies.

signatureTracks.title: Buddy (Remix)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Brought Q-Tip, Jungle Brothers, Queen Latifah and Monie Love together as the Native Tongues' clearest single statement.
